41270681.model_family: dual-U-Net convolutional network with atlas prior and spatial attention

41270681.patient_population: fetuses undergoing brain MRI across a range of gestational ages (in-house and two public datasets)
41270681.model_description: AtlasSeg takes fetal brain MRI along with a publicly available gestational-age-specific brain atlas as input and outputs a seven-tissue segmentation map. 41270681.dataset_size: in-house dataset plus two public datasets (exact number not stated)
41270681.headline_result: highest average Dice similarity coefficient among ten compared networks
41270681.study_design: retrospective technical development and comparison against ten segmentation networks

41282032.exclusion_reason: review of regulatory/ethical pathways for pediatric radiopharmaceutical development; AI/radiomics mentioned only in passing among emerging technologies

41288534.clinical_problem: safe and effective adoption of AI tools across pediatric radiology practice
41288534.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing radiologic imaging generally
41288534.model_description: Multisociety position statement (ACR, ESPR, SPR, SLARP, AOSPR, SPIN) addressing four pillars of AI adoption in pediatric radiology: regulation and purchasing, implementation and integration, interpretation and postmarket surveillance, and education. It recommends pediatric-specific safety ratings, diverse pediatric training datasets, transparency metrics, explainability, phased implementation with pilot testing, postmarket surveillance, and AI literacy training for pediatric radiology staff.

41296158.exclusion_reason: non-radiologic imaging (corneal topography/tomography in keratoconus), ophthalmic biomarker review

41300569.exclusion_reason: clinical/ultrasound-marker-based prediction model (logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, neural net on tabular features), not image-based AI; no image analysis performed

41310360.model_family: deep learning segmentation (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet) and CNN classification with segmentation-informed pretraining
41310360.clinical_problem: noninvasive pretreatment prediction of BRAF mutation status in pediatric low-grade glioma
41310360.patient_population: 455 patients with pediatric low-grade glioma (pLGG) treated 1999-2023 at a children's hospital
41310360.model_description: Whole-brain FLAIR MRI is segmented by one of three tested networks (TransBTS, MedNeXt, MedicalNet) and then classified by a deep learning model to predict BRAF status without relying on manual tumor segmentation. A pretraining step embeds segmentation knowledge into the whole-brain classification model to improve accuracy without needing a tumor mask at inference.
41310360.dataset_size: 455 patients with molecularly characterized pLGG and whole-brain FLAIR MRI
41310360.headline_result: AUC 0.741 without segmentation knowledge, improved to 0.772 with segmentation pretraining (vs 0.756 for segmentation-based baseline)
41310360.study_design: retrospective single-center model development and comparison

41310564.exclusion_reason: dental age estimation (dentomaxillofacial panoramic radiographs), non-radiologic dental imaging excluded per scope

41312172.model_family: 2.5D deep learning combining Residual Network and Swin Transformer
41312172.clinical_problem: preoperative differentiation of pediatric posterior fossa tumor type (pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, ependymoma)

41312172.model_description: ResSwinT takes five-sequence MRI (T1WI, T1C, T2WI, FLAIR, ADC) constructed as 2.5D images and outputs a three-way classification among pilocytic astrocytoma, medulloblastoma, and ependymoma. SHAP analysis is used to show which tumor regions drive each prediction.

41317206.model_family: review of ML/deep learning post-processing tools (MELD-Graph, MAP18, FLAT1, SUPR-FLAIR)
41317206.clinical_problem: detecting subtle cortical abnormalities (e.g., focal cortical dysplasia) for presurgical planning in drug-resistant pediatric epilepsy

41317206.model_description: Narrative review of structural MRI post-processing tools for pediatric epilepsy surgery, including MELD-Graph (deep neural network surface-based lesion detection), MAP18 (voxel-based morphometry), FLAT1 (FLAIR/T1 ratio mapping) and SUPR-FLAIR (normalized FLAIR projection), describing how each increases sensitivity for focal cortical dysplasia and other subtle lesions when standard MRI appears normal.

41351630.clinical_problem: diagnosis, monitoring and management of congenital and acquired pediatric heart disease using cardiac CT and MRI
41351630.patient_population: children with congenital and acquired heart disease
41351630.model_description: Review of current and emerging AI applications in pediatric cardiac CT and MRI, covering image acquisition, segmentation, interpretation, diagnosis and outcome-prediction modeling, plus emerging directions such as multimodal risk stratification, digital twins, 3D modeling and computational fluid dynamics.

41355354.exclusion_reason: review of precision medicine (genetics, biomarkers, revascularization) in Moyamoya vasculopathy across all ages; AI-based diagnostics mentioned only briefly and in passing

41359272.clinical_problem: using AI to triage patients and optimize workflow in pediatric imaging departments
41359272.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing radiology department imaging
41359272.model_description: Review of machine-learning-based algorithms for pediatric radiology triage and workflow optimization, including clinical referral appropriateness, exam scheduling, protocoling, radiation dose reduction, and follow-up reminders, and discussion of limited pediatric training data and multimodal (imaging plus genomic and clinical) datasets as a path forward.

41359722.model_family: HRNet + Swin-Transformer deep learning framework with SVD-based curve analysis
41359722.clinical_problem: automated Cobb angle measurement and vertebral wedging assessment for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis severity
41359722.patient_population: patients aged 10-18 years with full-spine anteroposterior radiographs for scoliosis
41359722.model_description: The model takes full-spine anteroposterior radiographs and predicts superior and inferior endplate angles and vertebral midpoints for each vertebra, combining an HRNet/Swin-Transformer backbone with singular value decomposition to compute Cobb angle and a new Vertebral Wedging Index without assuming a predefined curve pattern.

41359722.study_design: retrospective model development with dual-rater annotation

41367603.exclusion_reason: narrative review of pediatric GI endoscopy; non-radiologic imaging (endoscopy), AI mentioned only as a brief future direction

41377877.exclusion_reason: adult breast cancer population (invasive ductal carcinoma), not pediatric

41393607.exclusion_reason: systematic review of AI in traumatic brain injury across all ages; pediatric applications described only as exploratory subset, not the focus

41395634.model_family: U-Net++ segmentation plus binary CNN classifier (2-step deep learning pipeline)
41395634.clinical_problem: detecting Monteggia fracture dislocations (radial head dislocation with ulnar fracture) on pediatric elbow radiographs
41395634.patient_population: pediatric patients with elbow radiographs used to train/test the pipeline (320 for segmentation, 157 for classification)
41395634.model_description: A two-step deep learning pipeline: a U-Net++ network segments the capitellum and radial neck on AP and lateral elbow radiographs to algorithmically compute radiocapitellar line displacement, and a separate binary classifier detects associated ulnar fractures, together flagging Monteggia fracture dislocations.
41395634.dataset_size: 320 AP/lateral elbow radiographs for segmentation; 157 paired radiographs for ulnar fracture classification
41395634.headline_result: radial head displacement detection sensitivity 92.3-100%, specificity 96.3-96.9%; ulnar fracture detection accuracy 87.5%, AUC 0.923
41395634.study_design: retrospective single-center diagnostic model development and validation

41397997.exclusion_reason: placental MRI texture analysis using linear regression models, not a trained AI/ML classifier; studies maternal exposure, not fetal/child diagnosis

41402819.model_family: causal forest algorithm with AI-quantified CT features
41402819.clinical_problem: identifying which children with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia are most likely to benefit from flexible bronchoscopy
41402819.patient_population: pediatric MPP patients, derivation cohort n=753, validation cohort n=139, two centers
41402819.model_description: A causal forest model combines clinical, laboratory and AI-quantified CT features (consolidation/atelectasis volume, pneumonia attenuation, consolidation ratio) to estimate each patient's individual treatment effect from flexible bronchoscopy, identifying a subgroup that benefits from the procedure (reduced fever duration) versus one that does not.
41402819.release_evidence: an accessible online tool of this model facilitates practical clinical implementation
41402819.headline_result: fever duration reduced in FB-beneficial subgroup: beta=-1.16 (derivation, p<0.001), beta=-0.68 (validation, p=0.04)

41407887.model_family: meta-analysis comparing echocardiography, biomarkers, miRNA and AI models
41407887.clinical_problem: early detection of subclinical anthracycline-induced cardiotoxicity in childhood cancer survivors
41407887.patient_population: childhood cancer survivors treated with anthracyclines (73 studies in qualitative synthesis, 10 in meta-analysis)
41407887.model_description: Systematic review and meta-analysis pooling the prognostic accuracy of echocardiography (global longitudinal strain), serum biomarkers, microRNAs, and AI-based models for predicting chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity in pediatric cancer patients; AI-based models had the highest pooled predictive AUC among the modalities compared.
41407887.headline_result: pooled AUC ~0.80 for AI-based models vs ~0.72 for global longitudinal strain

41431395.clinical_problem: improving prenatal detection of congenital heart disease on obstetric ultrasound
41431395.patient_population: fetuses undergoing obstetric ultrasound screening for congenital heart disease
41431395.model_description: Review of AI applications in fetal cardiac ultrasound, including automated standard-view acquisition, congenital heart disease detection, and cardiac biometry, plus emerging generative AI, self-supervised learning, and NLP-based report automation.
41431395.headline_result: AI has shown expert-level performance in view classification, CHD detection, and cardiac biometry (as reported by cited literature)

41437729.clinical_problem: overcoming motion, low signal-to-noise ratio, and slice misregistration limitations of fetal MRI
41437729.model_description: Review of AI applications in fetal MRI: image reconstruction, denoising, motion correction, automated segmentation, and quantitative analysis including gestational-age estimation and anomaly detection, noting that most studies use small single-center datasets with limited external validation.

41477272.exclusion_reason: diagnostic accuracy study of expert radiologist chest radiograph interpretation for pediatric TB; no AI/ML model evaluated, AI mentioned only as a future direction

41602239.exclusion_reason: narrative review of AI/AR across orthopedic surgery generally; pediatrics mentioned only as one of several subspecialties, not the focus

41624879.model_family: YOLO-based segmentation with radiomics and Random Forest classifier
41624879.clinical_problem: early diagnosis of hip synovitis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis
41624879.patient_population: children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis undergoing hip ultrasound (internal and external validation cohorts)
41624879.model_description: YOLO-JIA automatically segments hip ultrasound images; radiomic features are extracted from the segmented regions and selected via ANOVA/LASSO, then classified by a Random Forest model to identify early hip synovitis in juvenile idiopathic arthritis. 41624879.dataset_size: not stated precisely (internal and external validation sets)
41624879.headline_result: YOLO-JIA precision 0.98, recall 1.00, mAP50-95 0.86; Random Forest AUC 0.88 internal, 0.81 external
41624879.study_design: retrospective model development with internal and external validation

41624918.exclusion_reason: review of non-invasive prenatal testing via cell-free fetal DNA; non-imaging genetic screening

41625753.clinical_problem: detection and management of fetal growth restriction and macrosomia
41625753.patient_population: fetuses assessed for growth restriction, small/large-for-gestational-age, and macrosomia
41625753.model_description: Comprehensive review of AI applications for fetal growth disorders, including automated ultrasound biometry, prediction models combining maternal/fetal biomarkers and Doppler indices, and deep learning applied directly to ultrasound images, noting most evidence is retrospective, small, and lacks external validation.

41625856.exclusion_reason: review of digital/internet addiction; not radiology imaging

41648050.exclusion_reason: narrative review of predictors of pediatric ESWL outcome; AI-based models mentioned only in passing among several predictor categories

41705231.exclusion_reason: narrative review of AI in pediatric dentistry; non-radiologic dental imaging excluded per scope

41784243.exclusion_reason: clinical-variable prediction model (logistic regression/SVM on symptoms, labs, one US measurement) for surgical intervention; not an image-based AI model

41953470.model_family: deep learning brain segmentation framework using domain randomization

41953470.patient_population: infants and young children undergoing brain MRI with diverse, sometimes clinically acquired protocols
41953470.model_description: BabySeg is a deep learning segmentation model for infant and young-child brain MRI that supports diverse MRI protocols and image types not seen during training, including repeat scans, by training on synthetic images generated through domain randomization; it also flexibly pools features from any number of input scans.

38221885.model_family: convolutional neural network (segmentation) plus custom measurement code
38221885.clinical_problem: automated measurement of lower limb alignment (mechanical/anatomic axes) in children
38221885.patient_population: children undergoing standing lower limb radiographs for skeletal pathology assessment
38221885.model_description: A CNN segments pediatric weight-bearing lower limb radiographs; custom code then extracts anatomic landmarks from the segmentation to automatically calculate mechanical axis deviation and other alignment angles, compared against manual measurements by orthopaedic fellows.
38221885.headline_result: mechanical axis deviation within mean 2.02 mm; lateral distal femoral angle mean deviation 1.73 degrees; ~2 seconds per radiograph
38221885.study_design: retrospective single-center model development compared to manual measurement

38227019.model_family: automated bone health index software (existing commercial AI tool)

38227019.patient_population: 434 healthy children ages 3-15 (214 European-Caucasian, 220 North African) with normal hand/wrist radiographs
38227019.model_description: BoneXpert, a commercial automated software, processes left-hand/wrist radiographs to compute the Bone Health Index (BHI) and its standard-deviation score, which are compared with manually calculated Exton-Smith Index values to establish ethnicity-specific normative ranges.
38227019.headline_result: mean BHI lower in North African children (4.23/4.17) than European Caucasian (4.50/4.68), P<0.001; BHI variability <15% regardless of age/ethnicity

38232121.model_family: CNN ensembles (Cold-start, Warm-start, Shrink-and-Perturb initialization; F-SLSQP and attention-guided fuzzy softmax ensembles)

38232121.model_description: The study compares three ways of initializing deep CNN weights (cold-start, warm-start, shrink-and-perturb) for chest X-ray classification models retrained periodically as new data arrive, evaluating generalization to external adult and pediatric datasets, and proposes new ensembling methods that combine weights from multiple models.
38232121.dataset_size: multiple public adult and pediatric CXR datasets
38232121.headline_result: ImageNet-pretrained models generalized better; weight-level ensembles showed significantly higher recall (p<0.05)

38262691.exclusion_reason: lipoprotein profiling by NMR spectroscopy for genetic testing yield in familial hypercholesterolemia; non-imaging laboratory biomarker study

38266514.exclusion_reason: fMRI mediation analysis of social victimization and psychosis-like experiences; no machine learning model applied

38271993.model_family: deep learning bone age estimation software

38271993.patient_population: 371 healthy Korean children aged 4-17 undergoing routine health check-ups
38271993.model_description: A commercial deep-learning bone age software (BoneAge, Vuno) analyzes left-hand radiographs to estimate bone age, which is compared against chronological age using concordance rate and Bland-Altman analysis in healthy children.
38271993.release_evidence: commercial deep-learning-based BA software (BoneAge, Vuno, Seoul, Korea)

38277807.clinical_problem: predicting hand motor function after neonatal arterial ischemic stroke from brain MRI structure

38277807.model_description: Structural T1-weighted MRI is used to build graphs representing basal ganglia and thalamus volumes, elongations, and distances; a graph neural network performs graph regression to predict Box and Blocks Test hand motor function scores for both hands after neonatal stroke.
38277807.dataset_size: 35 children with neonatal arterial ischemic stroke
38277807.headline_result: significant correlation between predicted and actual score ratios (p<0.05), mean L1 distance <0.03

38279605.clinical_problem: identifying single umbilical artery (umbilical cord vascular anomaly) on prenatal ultrasound
38279605.patient_population: retrospectively collected prenatal ultrasound images of umbilical cord (expanded dataset of 286 images)
38279605.model_description: Ultrasound images of the umbilical cord are preprocessed (text removal via AI-based OCR) and classified by a ResNet34 convolutional neural network to detect single umbilical artery, an anomaly, versus normal three-vessel cords.

38323184.patient_population: 278 four-chamber-view fetal echocardiography images (normal, AVSD, and differential diagnosis groups)
38323184.model_description: U-Net, MA-Net and Link-Net models are trained to automatically detect seven anatomical landmarks on fetal echocardiographic four-chamber views, from which atrial and ventricular length are measured to compute the AL/VL ratio (AVLR) used to diagnose atrioventricular septal defect.

38350787.clinical_problem: automatically organizing fetal ultrasound images into standard views without manual labeling
38350787.patient_population: second-trimester fetal ultrasound scans, 88,063 images for development and 8,187 unseen images for evaluation
38350787.model_description: FUSC uses unsupervised, self-supervised deep learning to automatically cluster large volumes of second-trimester fetal ultrasound images into different fetal anatomical views, removing the need for manual labeling of scan images.

38350787.dataset_size: 88,063 images for development, 8,187 images for evaluation

38365300.model_family: planned committee of deep learning and statistical learning algorithms

38365300.model_description: Protocol for developing an intelligent decision-support system (PARADISE) that will use 2D ultrasound video from the standard second-trimester morphology scan to guide probe acquisition, automatically detect and measure fetal anatomical planes, and flag unusual findings suggestive of congenital anomalies; the system has not yet been built or tested.
38365300.release_evidence: protocol for the development of an intelligent decision support system; training phase where the system learns
38365300.dataset_size: planned enrollment of 4000 patients over 32 months

38401893.model_family: planned convolutional neural network for 3D ultrasound bone age segmentation and prediction
38401893.clinical_problem: radiation-free bone age assessment using 3D ultrasound compared with radiographic bone age
38401893.patient_population: children referred to a pediatric growth and development clinic, receiving paired hand 3D-ultrasound and X-ray
38401893.model_description: Protocol for a prospective diagnostic accuracy study that will use a novel automatic 3D-ultrasound hand scanning device with a CNN-based cascade network to segment hand skeletal structures and predict bone age directly from 3D ultrasound images, compared against paediatrician-read radiographic bone age.
38401893.release_evidence: protocol for a prospective, diagnostic accuracy study; new, safer, radiation-free BA assessment method

38405710.model_description: Built with generative AI, the μBrain atlas is a 3D cellular-resolution digital reference combining postmortem 21-week fetal brain serial sections with bulk tissue microarray gene-expression data across 29 cortical regions; it is used to relate molecular signatures to cortical expansion rates measured in utero with MRI.

38405710.study_design: preprint; atlas development and cross-modal analysis

38467666.patient_population: 97 growth-restricted and 111 normally grown singleton fetuses, 24-37 weeks gestation
38467666.model_description: Doppler ultrasound waveforms of the pulmonary vessels, taken before and after maternal hyperoxygenation, are classified into clusters by machine learning and fed into a computational model that estimates the ratio of pulmonary vascular resistance before and after oxygenation, distinguishing responsive from non-responsive growth-restricted fetuses.
38467666.headline_result: cluster A PVR ratio 0.98±0.33 vs cluster B 0.78±0.28, p=0.0156

38494431.model_family: adaptive wavelet noise suppression (AWNS) plus supervised machine learning classifier (Naive Bayes)
38494431.clinical_problem: classifying pediatric brain tumor type (ependymoma, medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma) from proton MR spectroscopy

38527503.model_family: LASSO feature selection with random forest classifier

38527503.model_description: Lung ultrasound signs (consolidation, confluent B-lines, pleural effusion) are selected by LASSO regression and fed into a random forest classifier to diagnose pneumonia (against chest CT) and to predict severe disease in hospitalized children.

38527503.headline_result: AUC 0.87 (full variables) / 0.84 (LASSO-selected) for CAP diagnosis; AUC 0.76 for severe CAP using consolidation size/body surface area

38621854.model_family: deep learning architectures with data augmentation (literature review plus methodology)

38621854.model_description: The paper reviews and proposes advanced deep learning architectures with data augmentation techniques for diagnosing and predicting fetal conditions, including Down syndrome, from ultrasound images, discussing training/validation processes and clinical translation considerations.

38647355.exclusion_reason: maternal thyroid ultrasound classification in women; not a pediatric imaging study (fetal neurodevelopment discussed only as rationale)

38659641.headline_result: F1 0.606 for interim residual disease detection; Dice 0.772 baseline segmentation; Spearman's rho 0.78-0.96 vs physician measurements

38767532.exclusion_reason: adult women with pelvic organ prolapse; not a pediatric population

38824518.clinical_problem: identifying surgical target areas (osteomyelitis, abscess) in pediatric hip and periarticular infections

38824518.dataset_size: 7970 axial STIR MRI images from 275 patients (three hospitals)
38824518.headline_result: AUC 0.810 (osteomyelitis) and 0.890 (abscess); accuracy 0.976 and 0.957, statistically better than four surgeons (P<0.05); 0.2 s per image vs 10 s for specialists
38824518.study_design: retrospective multicenter model development and comparison

38831258.model_family: logistic regression, classification tree, and random forest models
38831258.clinical_problem: predicting pulmonary metastases to qualify children and adolescents with osteosarcoma for thoracotomy
38831258.patient_population: 64 pediatric osteosarcoma patients suspected of lung metastases on CT, 100 thoracotomies
38831258.model_description: CT scans of osteosarcoma patients are evaluated for nodule number, size, calcification and location; logistic regression, classification tree and random forest models are built from these CT-derived features to predict which patients truly have pulmonary metastases, aiming to reduce unnecessary thoracotomies.
38831258.headline_result: sensitivity 72-92%, positive predictive value 81-90%, accuracy 74-79% across models

38836466.model_family: deep-learning-based synthetic MRI generation for surface-based morphometry
38836466.clinical_problem: characterizing supratentorial cortical and subcortical morphological changes caused by pediatric infratentorial (posterior fossa) tumors
38836466.patient_population: 24 patients aged 4-18 years with primary infratentorial tumors and 41 matched healthy controls
38836466.model_description: Synthetic MPRAGE-like images are generated with deep learning algorithms from T2-axial brain MRI, then used to automatically calculate cortical thickness, surface area, volume, local gyrification index, and subcortical gray matter volumes, comparing pediatric infratentorial tumor patients with healthy controls.
38836466.headline_result: cortical thinning in left supramarginal gyrus; volume reduction in several left-hemisphere gyri (P<0.05)

38840678.model_family: radiomics with logistic regression and quadratic discriminant analysis
38840678.clinical_problem: distinguishing diffuse large B-cell lymphoma from Hodgkin's lymphoma in children using enhanced CT
38840678.model_description: 2264 radiomics features are extracted from enhanced CT images of pediatric lymphoma lesions, reduced by correlation/mRMR/LASSO, and used to build logistic regression and quadratic discriminant analysis models, with and without the clinical marker LDH, to non-invasively distinguish DLBCL from Hodgkin's lymphoma.
38840678.headline_result: AUC 0.814-0.845 across radiomics and radiomics+LDH models

38847850.exclusion_reason: graph-theoretic multilayer network analysis of structural/diffusion MRI, not a trained AI/ML predictive model

38853782.clinical_problem: predicting clinically significant outcomes (worsening dilation, UTI, impaired renal function) in infants with ureteropelvic junction obstruction
38853782.patient_population: 28 children with UPJO followed prospectively in the first year of life
38853782.model_description: Antenatal and postnatal renal ultrasound findings (UTD classification and anteroposterior pelvic diameter, both graded by a blinded pediatric radiologist) are compared using ROC-AUC and Random Forest analysis to predict which infants with UPJO will have a clinically significant event within the first year of life.
38853782.headline_result: antenatal APD >15 mm most predictive marker, AUC=0.867

38872737.exclusion_reason: editorial with empty abstract; content and relevance to radiology AI cannot be determined

38873338.model_family: Vision Transformer with Federated Self-Supervised Learning
38873338.clinical_problem: binary COVID-19 versus non-COVID-19 classification on pediatric chest X-rays
38873338.patient_population: pediatric chest X-ray patients (exact cohort size not stated in abstract)
38873338.model_description: CAFES pre-trains a Vision Transformer using federated self-supervised learning on adult chest X-ray data across a privacy-preserving federated computing platform, then fine-tunes it to classify pediatric chest X-rays as COVID-19 or non-COVID-19.
38873338.headline_result: AUPR 0.952, 0.231 points higher than fully supervised model

38900321.clinical_problem: assessing pediatric peripheral neuroblastic tumor cell behavior (pathological subtype and histology group) noninvasively
38900321.patient_population: 81 pediatric patients with peripheral neuroblastic tumors, undergoing contrast-enhanced CT and MRI
38900321.model_description: Radiomics features are extracted from contrast-enhanced CT and from T1WI/T2WI MRI of segmented neuroblastic tumors, and separate radiomics models compare the ability of CT versus MRI features to distinguish pathological subtype (neuroblastoma vs ganglioneuroblastoma/ganglioneuroma) and INPC histology group.
38900321.headline_result: CECT radiomics AUC 0.765-0.870 (subtype) vs MRI radiomics AUC 0.549-0.748

38929793.clinical_problem: AI detection and quantification of injured liver area after trauma, sepsis, or chemotherapy
38929793.patient_population: 564 patients across 6 studies, including 170 (30%) pediatric patients
38929793.model_description: Review of six studies applying AI/radiomics to CT (five studies) and FAST ultrasound (one study) to detect and quantify acute liver injury from trauma, sepsis, or chemotherapy, in cohorts combining adult and pediatric patients; most studies reported specificity over 80%.

38949769.clinical_problem: whether AI can detect hard-to-identify fetal cardiac anomalies on obstetric ultrasound
38949769.model_description: Editorial/comment discussing whether artificial intelligence can detect difficult-to-identify fetal cardiac anomalies on obstetric ultrasound; abstract text not provided, so specific findings are unknown.

38963574.exclusion_reason: published erratum/correction notice with no abstract content

38972309.exclusion_reason: salivary metabolite/protein biomarker study for dental caries risk; non-imaging

38994451.clinical_problem: imaging assessment of fetal membrane abnormalities and their relation to adverse perinatal outcomes
38994451.patient_population: pregnant patients undergoing prenatal fetal membrane imaging
38994451.model_description: Review of imaging methods (ultrasound and other modalities) for assessing fetal membrane abnormalities such as thickening and separation, and their relation to adverse perinatal outcomes, with discussion of the future role of artificial intelligence in fetal membrane imaging.

39008780.clinical_problem: achieving accurate, efficient fetal brain MRI segmentation based on true physical scan resolution rather than upsampled apparent resolution
39008780.model_description: ConvNet segmentation models are evaluated on brain MRI downsampled to its true acquisition (physical) resolution rather than the higher apparent resolution used clinically; for fetal brain MRI, images were downsampled per estimated physical resolution before segmentation and restored via upsampling, showing negligible accuracy loss with much smaller, faster models.
39008780.headline_result: accuracy reduced by only 0.26-1.8% with downsampling factors of 4/3 to 4; models up to 7x smaller and 10x faster

39011367.model_family: twelve machine learning algorithms compared (best: random forest)
39011367.clinical_problem: using brain volumetric measurements to predict adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
39011367.patient_population: 32 patients with severe AIS and 31 healthy individuals
39011367.model_description: Volumetric measurements from 169 brain regions on MRI are used as predictors in twelve machine learning algorithms (random forest performing best) to classify adolescent idiopathic scoliosis versus healthy controls, identifying corticospinal tract and cerebellar volumes as most important.

39017730.exclusion_reason: dental panoramic radiograph analysis (mesiodens detection); non-radiologic dental imaging excluded per scope

39040082.clinical_problem: classifying Doppler ultrasound signal type to improve fetal heart rate tracing during monitoring
39040082.patient_population: fetal Doppler ultrasound signals from non-stress tests and labor monitoring
39040082.model_description: A semi-supervised CNN is trained on labeled and unlabeled Doppler ultrasound signal segments (fetal heartbeat, artifact, and two other categories) from cardiotocography monitoring, aiming to classify signal type and improve continuous fetal heart rate tracing beyond the standard autocorrelation algorithm.

39052572.model_family: convolutional neural network (pneumonia classification), trained on adult data
39052572.clinical_problem: whether adult-trained CNNs can classify pneumonia on pediatric chest radiographs despite limited pediatric training data
39052572.patient_population: 5,856 pediatric chest X-rays (ages 1-5) for evaluation; 46,947 adult chest X-rays for training
39052572.model_description: A pneumonia-classification CNN is trained exclusively on 46,947 curated adult chest X-rays, with thoracic segmentation preprocessing to reduce attention outside the thorax, and then evaluated for its ability to discriminate pneumonia on a separate pediatric chest X-ray dataset without pediatric-specific retraining.
39052572.headline_result: pneumonia discrimination AUC 0.95 on adult test set, AUC 0.82 on pediatric dataset

39061217.model_family: Random Forest machine learning classifier with SMOTE balancing
39061217.clinical_problem: discriminating pediatric posterior fossa tumor subtype using diffusion kurtosis imaging
39061217.patient_population: 34 children (mean age 7.48 years) with posterior fossa tumors (medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, ependymoma)
39061217.model_description: Whole-tumor and region-of-interest diffusion kurtosis imaging metrics are compared for measurement repeatability, then whole-tumor (VOI-based) DKI metrics from a SMOTE-balanced dataset are used to train a Random Forest classifier that discriminates medulloblastoma, pilocytic astrocytoma, and ependymoma.

39090235.model_family: bimodal model combining CNN image features with automatically-generated clinical measurements (aaCM); compared with LightGBM, XGBoost, SVM, single CNN
39090235.clinical_problem: diagnosing hip instability (developmental dysplasia of the hip) in infants at risk
39090235.patient_population: 813 radiographic hip images of infants at risk of DDH (232 unstable, 581 stable), multicenter
39090235.model_description: The model automatically generates clinical measurements (an automatic algorithm for clinical measurement, aaCM) from radiographic hip images of infants and integrates these with CNN image features in a bimodal model, to classify hips as stable or unstable, benchmarked against provocative-examination ground truth and specialist accuracy.
39090235.headline_result: aaCM accuracy equal to or higher than specialists; bimodal model outperformed LightGBM, XGBoost, SVM, single CNN

39152359.model_family: deep learning machine learning models (rod model, 58 mm model, head-piece model)
39152359.clinical_problem: automatically measuring magnetically controlled growing rod length adjustments on radiographs in early-onset scoliosis
39152359.patient_population: children with early-onset scoliosis treated with magnetically controlled growing rods
39152359.model_description: Three deep-learning models (rod, 58 mm reference, and head-piece detection) are combined to automatically extract growing rod length from posteroanterior spine radiographs, compared against manual measurements for accuracy, reliability, and speed.
39152359.dataset_size: 387 radiographs for development; 60 radiographs (118 rods) for testing
39152359.headline_result: average precision 67.6-94.8% across models; MAD 0.98±0.88 mm; ICC 0.90; 6.1 s per measurement

39154805.exclusion_reason: DXA-derived body composition outcomes analyzed with Bayesian regression/gradient boosting on nutrition intake variables; not an image-analysis AI model

39155321.model_family: random forest classifier atlas-based segmentation with expectation-maximization Markov random field
39155321.clinical_problem: segmenting gray matter, white matter and CSF on neonatal brain MRI
39155321.patient_population: 40 neonatal MR images, gestational age 37-44 weeks
39155321.model_description: A subject-specific atlas is generated using a random forest classifier, then combined with an expectation-maximization Markov random field method to segment gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid on neonatal brain MRI, using intensity- and gradient-based features.
39155321.headline_result: overall accuracy 94.3%, Dice 0.945 (GM), 0.947 (WM), 0.912 (CSF); up to 4% improvement over comparator methods

39163826.model_family: transformer combining variational autoencoder embeddings, ResNet-18 features, and patient metadata
39163826.clinical_problem: detecting lung consolidations on pediatric lung ultrasound video for pneumonia diagnosis
39163826.patient_population: pediatric lung ultrasound pneumonia patients (video-level dataset, size not specified in abstract)
39163826.model_description: FLUEnT combines frame-level embeddings from a variational autoencoder, spatial features from a ResNet-18, and encoded patient metadata into fused encodings that are passed to a transformer for binary classification of lung consolidation presence in pediatric lung ultrasound videos.
39163826.headline_result: mean balanced accuracy 89.3%, outperforming state-of-the-art models by an average of 8 percentage points

39167356.clinical_problem: identifying distinct patterns of normal sagittal spinal alignment in adolescents
39167356.patient_population: 111 normal adolescent sagittal spine radiographs from a single pediatric institution
39167356.model_description: Multiple semi-supervised machine learning clustering algorithms are applied to sagittal spinal alignment parameters measured from adolescent spine radiographs to determine whether normal sagittal alignment forms distinct subgroups, rather than a single continuum.
39167356.headline_result: 3-5 optimal clusters identified; sagittal vertical axis (SVA) most significantly distinguished clusters

39171131.model_family: mask conditional diffusion model (generative deep learning)
39171131.clinical_problem: generating synthetic training images of classic metaphyseal lesions, a fracture highly specific to infant abuse, to augment limited training data
39171131.patient_population: 39 infants (mean age 4.1 months) with distal tibia radiographs, used to derive real and synthetic test images
39171131.model_description: A mask conditional diffusion model (MaC-DM) generates synthetic distal tibia radiographs with and without classic metaphyseal lesions to augment a limited training dataset for automated fracture detection; three blinded radiologists then assessed whether the synthetic images correctly showed the lesion and whether they could distinguish real from synthetic images.
39171131.dataset_size: 100 real images tested (from 177 normal/73 CML dataset); 100 synthetic images generated
39171131.headline_result: radiologists diagnosed CML with kappa 0.90, accuracy 92%, but could not distinguish real from synthetic images (kappa 0.05, accuracy 53%)
39171131.study_design: retrospective single-center generative model development with reader study

39180859.model_family: fine-grained deep convolutional neural network architecture with LION optimizer and Grad-CAM
39180859.clinical_problem: recognizing pediatric wrist pathologies, particularly fractures, on trauma X-rays
39180859.patient_population: children and adolescents with wrist trauma radiographs (limited dataset)
39180859.model_description: A fine-grained deep convolutional neural network automatically identifies discriminative regions in pediatric wrist X-rays to classify wrist pathologies, refined via ablation analysis and the LION optimizer, with Grad-CAM used to visualize the regions driving each prediction.
39180859.dataset_size: limited dataset (exact size not stated in abstract)
39180859.headline_result: accuracy 86% (augmented) and 84% (original) test sets; fracture sensitivity 97%

39217235.model_family: deep learning-based annotation program vs conventional semi-automated region-growing
39217235.clinical_problem: reproducibility of ventricular volume measurement on cardiac CT in pediatric congenital heart disease
39217235.patient_population: 127 patients (mean age 82.1 months) undergoing pediatric protocol cardiac CT
39217235.model_description: A deep learning-based annotation program (DLS) automatically segments left/right ventricular or functional single-ventricle volumes on pediatric cardiac CT and is compared against a conventional semi-automated region-growing tool (CM), assessing intra-observer, inter-observer, and interstudy reproducibility as well as time to reconstruct across three readers.
39217235.release_evidence: deep learning-based annotation program (DLS, Medilabel, Ingradient, Inc., Seoul, Republic of Korea)
39217235.headline_result: DLS showed better inter/intra-observer agreement and significantly shorter reconstruction time than conventional method

39256746.model_family: deep learning model based on nnU-Net architecture
39256746.clinical_problem: pretherapeutic differentiation of germinoma versus nongerminomatous germ cell tumor subtype and prognosis in pediatric intracranial germ cell tumors
39256746.patient_population: 280 pathologically confirmed pediatric intracranial germ cell tumor patients (training/internal test), plus prospective and two external test cohorts
39256746.model_description: iGNet, based on the nnU-Net architecture, analyzes pretherapeutic T2-weighted MRI to classify intracranial germ cell tumors as germinoma or nongerminomatous germ cell tumor, and its output is also evaluated for predicting progression-free and overall survival; six neuroradiologists' diagnostic accuracy was compared with and without iGNet assistance.
39256746.dataset_size: 280 patients (training/internal test); prospective n=22; external n=22 and n=20
39256746.headline_result: AUC 0.869-0.950 across four test datasets; radiologist AUC improved 9.22-17.90% with AI assistance
39256746.study_design: retrospective/prospective multicentre model development and reader study

39274294.model_family: six machine learning models compared, best XGBoost
39274294.clinical_problem: predicting prognosis (seizure relapse) in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy using clinical and MRI features
39274294.patient_population: patients with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy at a single hospital (age not specified in abstract)
39274294.model_description: Clinical variables and MRI-derived brain region volumes (e.g., left cerebellum white matter, right thalamus, left globus pallidus) are combined and used to train six machine learning models, with XGBoost performing best, to predict prognosis in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy; SHAP analysis identifies the most influential features.
39274294.headline_result: XGBoost AUROC 0.700 combining clinical and MRI data

39294311.exclusion_reason: letter/commentary on pediatric head trauma imaging and radiation safety; AI mentioned only briefly as a future direction for dose reduction

39326769.model_family: deep learning brain age prediction with regional age prediction and perturbation-based saliency map interpretability methods
39326769.clinical_problem: interpretable prediction of neonatal brain age from structural MRI to identify regions relevant to premature brain development
39326769.patient_population: 664 T1-weighted neonatal MRI scans processed with the NEOCIVET pipeline
39326769.model_description: Brain surface and cortical features are extracted from neonatal T1 MRI using the NEOCIVET pipeline and fed into a deep learning brain-age prediction model; two interpretability methods (regional age prediction and perturbation-based saliency maps) are compared for identifying which brain regions drive age predictions, aiming toward more interpretable, personalized tools for premature neonates.
